misconceptions.description: Planning only the intended flow and omitting failure modes, access gaps, and responsibility
misconceptions.trigger: plan lists activities and logins but no fallback or owner when the tool fails
misconceptions.feedback: Add what happens when the tool fails or a student cannot access it, and name who is responsible at each step.

misconceptions.description: Scheduling an activity before the consent, training, or access gate it depends on
misconceptions.trigger: a required gate is scheduled after the activity that relies on it
misconceptions.feedback: Order the timeline so every gate clears before the activity that depends on it.

misconceptions.description: Adopting an AI-generated rollout schedule without reconciling it to local constraints
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses the model's schedule without checking the real calendar, devices, or consent timeline
misconceptions.feedback: Treat the generated schedule as a checklist, then adjust it to the constraints the model could not see.

misconceptions.description: Defining rollout success as completion rather than as a learning outcome with an equity guardrail
misconceptions.trigger: success criterion is everyone finishes the module
misconceptions.feedback: Define success as a learning gain plus a check that no subgroup falls further behind, so the plan is evaluable.
